bio:
William F. Meier was born about 1904 in Tamaqua, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, where his family was living in 1905 and 1906; the records disagree on the exact year, placing it between 1903 and 1905. He was the son of Henry J. Meier, a German-born iron moulder, and Anna Higgins. His brothers and sisters were Fred Aloysius (1892–1966), Henry James Jr. (1894–1957), Mary C. (1897–1962), Madeline Edelberta (1900–1995) and Joseph John (1906–1970); one more child had died by 1910. By 1910 the family had moved to Mill Street in Wilkes-Barre, and in 1920, at 15, William was an errand boy at a drug store while living with his parents on Barney Street.

On 20 April 1926, in Wilkes-Barre, he married Florence Louise Pringle, a clerk born in Plymouth and the daughter of the carpenter Addison Pringle and Catherine Heffernan; William was then a clerk of 22 living on Barney Street, and the Rev. D. W. McCarthy performed the ceremony. By 1930 he was a clerk in a coal office, living on Cedar Street with Florence and their sons William and James, close to the Pringle family on Huston Street. In 1950 he was a supervisor at a coal company, still on Cedar Street, with Florence, William Jr., James C. and Barbara Ann. His father Henry lived on until December 1950, dying at 83 on Barney Street, when William was 46. The Florence Irene Meier buried from Wilkes-Barre in October 1933 was not his daughter but his niece, the 17-year-old eldest child of his brother Fred Aloysius Meier and Anna Mather.

William died in Wilkes-Barre on 4 July 1963, aged 59. He is John's great-grandfather and the father of James C. Meier.

The family name was spelt Mayer in the Munzingen registers of Baden from 1820 to 1862, Meyer in the 1870 United States census and Myer in 1880; the first record to write it Meier was the 1892 marriage record of his father Henry J. Meier, written by the clerk, so Henry may not have chosen the spelling himself. From 1910 on it was consistently Meier, apart from a Meyer in the 1940 census, and no formal change of name was ever recorded.

researchNotes:
William F. Meier was born about 1904 in Tamaqua, Schuylkill County, PA (birthplace on his 1926 marriage application; his ages are 6 in Apr 1910, 15 in Jan 1920, 22 in Apr 1926, 26 in 1930, 45 in 1950 and 59 at death in Jul 1963). FamilySearch (LTHM-B3G) dates him 1905–1963; the Ancestry tree says 1904–1963. Henry's family was in Tamaqua in 1905–06 (brother Joseph John born there 30 Jun 1906). In 1910 he was 'William, son, 6' at 14 Mill Street, Wilkes-Barre Ward 14; in 1920 'William, son, 15, errand boy at a drug store' at 298 Barney St, Ward 15. On 16 Apr 1926 he swore marriage-licence application No. 10768 in Luzerne County: William F. Meier, clerk, born Tamaqua, PA, residing at 16 Barney St, Wilkes-Barre, age 22, not previously married; father 'Henry', residing in Wilkes-Barre, moulder, birthplace given as 'Penna.' (an error — Henry was German-born); mother 'Anna', maiden name 'Higgins'. The bride was Florence Louise Pringle, clerk, born Plymouth, of 28 Huston St, age 22, daughter of Addison (carpenter) and Catherine Heffernan. They married 20 Apr 1926, by Rev. D. W. McCarthy, Wilkes-Barre. In 1930 (ED 40-261, sheet 23B, 55 Cedar Street) he was 'Wm F., head, 26', clerk in a 'coal office', with Florence (25), William (about 3) and James (1 9/12); Addison Pringle's family at 28 Huston St is on the same census sheet. In 1950 (ED 40-102, sheet 2, house 55) he was 'William F., head, 45, supervisor at a coal company' (company abbreviation unclear), with Florence (45), William Jr. (23), James C. (21) and Barbara Ann (14). In 1943 'Mrs. William Meier' of Wilkes-Barre was listed among Addison Pringle's survivors (the only anchor found in the first report). He died 4 Jul 1963 in Wilkes-Barre (PA death index 1963: 'MEIER, WILLIAM F; age 59; WLKS BRE; county 40 [Luzerne]; died 07/04/63; file 071200; residence code 40001'). A search snippet also shows a 'William F Meier, b. 26 Dec 1905, d. 8 Jan 1964' and a 'William A. Meier, b. 1904, d. 10 Mar 1964 in Pennsylvania' — probably other men; the 1963 death is kept. His WWII draft card (1940s 'old man's' registration, b. 1904) was not reachable. Possible infant daughter: 'Meier, Florence Irene', funeral from Wilkes-Barre, notice published 11/12 Oct 1933 (not in the 1933 PA death index under M600; speculative).

The 'Florence Irene Meier' buried from Wilkes-Barre in October 1933 was not William's daughter. She was his niece, Florence Irene Meier (b. 15 Mar 1916 Wilkes-Barre, d. 9 Oct 1933 Wilkes-Barre, aged 17), the eldest child of his brother Fred Aloysius Meier Sr. and Anna Mather. The FamilySearch tree attaches her to Fred's household in the 1920 and 1930 censuses and to a Find a Grave index entry at St. Mary's Cemetery, Hanover Twp. ([R4-S1]). William's father Henry J. Meier did not die in 1940: he was still living, aged 83, at 16 Barney Street in the 1950 census ([R4-S2]). So William was 46 when his father died, in December 1950 (see Henry J. Meier).
